title: SSVEP Nakanishi 2015 dataset
description: A 12-class steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) dataset recorded from 9 healthy subjects using 8-channel EEG acquired at 256 Hz. This dataset was used to compare canonical correlation analysis (CCA)-based methods for SSVEP detection in brain-computer interface applications, demonstrating that individual calibration data significantly improves detection performance over standard CCA approaches.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a Biosemi ActiveTwo system with 8 channels (PO7, PO3, POz, PO4, PO8, O1, Oz, O2) at 256 Hz sampling rate. Subjects viewed a 4×3 matrix of flickering visual stimuli (6×6 cm each) at 60 cm viewing distance on a 1280×800 pixel monitor refreshed at 60 Hz. Each trial consisted of a 1-second cue period followed by 4 seconds of simultaneous stimulus flickering at frequencies ranging from 9.25 to 14.75 Hz with 0.5 Hz resolution. Data were preprocessed with zero-phase IIR bandpass filtering (6-80 Hz), with epochs extracted from 0.15 to 4.3 seconds to account for visual system latency.
